runners_data.name: Revich
runners_data.note: Consistent stayer with six runs of recent form showing repeated placings at 10f on Good ground — sim-going record of 0W3P tells a true story, but he stays well and Miss Georgia King's 5lb claim is useful from draw 9; a genuine threat in Scenario A if he can slot just off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Grey Fox
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter from a perfect draw 1, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) is relevant — he is racing in a slightly unfamiliar front-running role and the 0W2P sim-going record suggests he tends to get run down; Emma Lavelle's stable is 0/9 over the past 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Unreliable recent form (086/8-) and a last run just three days ago raises freshness questions; his natural inclination is to race at the back of the field, and though the map places him in midfield he is unlikely to be in that position in running — his chance depends heavily on a strong gallop he may not get here, and the STYLE_FIT flag reinforces the discount.|

runners_data.name: Three Yorkshiremen
runners_data.note: Has run exclusively on Soft or Standard surfaces in his last five starts and all recent form came on those conditions, making this Good ground a mild unknown; a prominent-style runner who could harry Grey Fox from draw 7 if so instructed, which would help closers.|

runners_data.name: Arundel
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 65 with winning form and a recent third on Soft over 10f — the youngest horse in the field and potentially the most unexposed over this 1m3½f trip; Mr Henry Callan is an amateur but Arundel's class edge gives him a fair chance if he handles the step up in trip.|

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with a win at 17f on Good in his recent history — the sim-going record of 1W2P from 11 runs is legitimate evidence he handles this surface; he holds up and needs the race run at a decent clip, which is not guaranteed with Grey Fox likely to take a soft lead.|

runners_data.name: Stintino Sunset
runners_data.note: The Scorecard selection, and the form figures justify it — four consecutive placings at 12f on Good ground, all from a midfield position, is exactly the profile this race shape suits; trainer Julia & Shelley Birkett have been 1/5 in the last 14 days and Mr Ross Birkett knows this horse well.|

runners_data.name: Shahbaz
runners_data.note: Six consecutive runs without a placing on Good going in the sim-going record (0W0P from 3 runs) is a red flag on this surface; Archie Watson's yard is 4/19 in 14 days which is positive, but Shahbaz has not won in 2026 and his recent form figures of 246667 show a downward trajectory.|

runners_data.name: The Pug
runners_data.note: Consistent but limited — five runs show no better than fourth, and the sim-going record on Good (0W0P from 4 runs) is uninspiring; prominent style suits the expected race shape in theory, but Mr Josh Myers holds a 7lb claim and is inexperienced, and The Pug's overall quality appears below the principals here.|

races.paceDynamic: Grey Fox is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Three Yorkshiremen and Revich as genuine prominent types to press from the outside, the early tempo over this 1m3½f Bath trip is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than scorching. Grey Fox can bowl along at a measured gallop, dictating terms from draw 1 without being seriously harassed, which classically sets up a scenario where the leader either converts or is collared only late. Applejack Poet is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more closing types than can all settle at the rear — in reality Applejack Poet will be towards the back of the field, not genuinely mid-pack, and Stintino Sunset and Cogital are the closers most likely to be tracking the pace in the positions the map shows. Given a single, uncontested pace-setter operating at a comfortable gallop on Good ground over a staying trip, this race shape heavily favours horses who can travel prominently or mid-division with cover and produce a sustained, honest finish — pure hold-up horses dependent on a true end-to-end gallop are at a disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grey Fox Controls, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Fox dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the field strings out behind, setting up a genuine stamina test in the straight.
scenarios.body: Grey Fox rolls along from draw 1 at a pace of his own choosing, and the race becomes a sustained staying contest over the final three furlongs on Bath's uphill finish; horses who have been travelling within themselves just behind the leader are perfectly positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Crumbles, Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Fox goes too fast for conditions or Three Yorkshiremen pushes the tempo, causing the early leaders to empty inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: An overly quick early pace would leave the front end vulnerable to genuine closers finishing through in the final stages; this benefits hold-up types who have been conserving energy throughout the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Revich Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Revich settles in a stalking position just off Grey Fox and produces his reliable staying effort to wear down the leader.
scenarios.body: Revich has solid recent form at this sort of trip on Good ground and is comfortable at 10f-plus, and from draw 9 he can slot into a prominent berth tracking the pace; he has placed consistently in similar conditions and a modest tempo suits his honest, grinding style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Arundel Travels Best
scenarios.trigger: If Arundel, the youngest and highest-rated horse in the field, finds his feet quickly under an amateur and outstays rivals in the straight.
scenarios.body: Arundel holds an OR of 65 — the highest in this field — and at just four years old has the most upside, and if Mr Henry Callan delivers him into contention turning for home the class edge could tell late; his stamina at this trip is mildly unknown but his 10f-12f form is solid.

watchPoints.text: Stintino Sunset's trainer has hit 1/5 in the last 14 days and the horse's four consecutive Good-ground placings at exactly this trip make it the most form-consistent runner in the race — watch whether it travels fluently in the early-to-mid stages.

Grey Fox holds a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.94 — if he fails to settle cleanly in front or is headed early by Three Yorkshiremen from draw 7, the expected controlled tempo will not materialise and the entire race shape changes.

Applejack Poet ran just three days ago and is a genuine hold-up type being shown in midfield on the map — watch where Miss Imogen Mathias actually positions him in the first half-mile, as his true closing style needs a stronger gallop than this field is likely to generate.

Cogital's win came at 17f on Good ground and he is the one confirmed closer with genuine evidence of handling a longer stamina test — if the pace quickens materially in the back straight, he becomes a more serious factor than his current form suggests.

Arundel holds the highest OR in the field at 65 and is by far the youngest at four — if Mr Henry Callan has been instructed to produce him late, the class margin over rivals rated 44-57 could be decisive in the final furlong of Bath's testing uphill finish.

runners_data.name: No Ordinary Joe
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old midfield settler whose sole win came over 20f on Good; the drop to 1m2f looks sharp, but his Bath visit (1 win from 1 over 20f Good) is relevant course form — he simply needs a shorter trip than he has recently shown he wants, making him a speculative each-way interest at best.

runners_data.name: Dialstone
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has finished second in both career starts including one on Good ground, showing a consistent placing profile; Rhys Clutterbuck takes the ride 38 days after his last run, and the step up to 1m2f from 10f looks a logical progression for a horse whose two runner-up efforts suggest he handles genuine competition well.

runners_data.name: Colonnade
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's three-year-old holds a clear pace advantage as the field's only confirmed front-runner, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that stepping from sprint distances to 1m2f represents a role change; his three recent form figures of 3-5-3 at 8f suggest he has the class to lead but may find the extra ground tests his ability to sustain that position to the line.

runners_data.name: Mathoura
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's three-year-old has placed twice from four starts on Good-to-Soft through Good, most recently running third over 10f Good — a directly comparable prep; Mason Paetel's 3lb claim is a practical asset in a small field, and Mathoura's consistent proximity to the pace makes him the obvious danger if the leader begins to weaken approaching the final climb.

runners_data.name: Soul Of Appin
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's four-year-old carries an UNKNOWN going flag and no recorded form string, meaning pace style, trip suitability and ground preference are all unquantifiable; Jack Callan takes the ride and Meehan's yard is 3/11 over 14 days — not without hope, but a complete unknown in a race with classier, better-exposed rivals.

runners_data.name: Indian Mary
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's three-year-old is tagged as a hold-up horse with a tendency to fade in the finish, which is a significant concern on Bath's stamina-sapping straight; her sole start produced an eighth over 10f on Tapeta, so Good turf and this trip are untested territory, and Laura Pearson will need to produce her much earlier than her style suggests if she is to play a role.

races.paceDynamic: Colonnade is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no other natural pace-setter to push him, shapes to bowl along at a comfortable, sustainable tempo around Bath's galloping 1m2f circuit. Mathoura and Dialstone are both mapped as Prominent-to-Midfield types, so the pace ahead of the main group is unlikely to be genuinely searching. That controlled tempo through the middle stages means the race is likely to develop into a test of finishing quality from the home turn rather than one of stamina or attrition. This shape most directly favours horses who can travel in behind the leader, pick up smoothly on the final climb, and sustain their effort to the line — a profile that suits Midfield closers with tactical speed over this trip on Good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Colonnade sets an uncontested, honest-but-not-fast pace and the race is decided by finishing quality in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Colonnade dictates from the front without pressure, keeping fractions moderate and leaving plenty in the tank for those tracking in behind; midfield runners who can close smoothly off the bridle are handed a straightforward opportunity to pounce. Good ground and Bath's stiff finish reward those with a clean turn of foot rather than raw stamina grinds.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Surprise, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Colonnade goes too hard early without cover and ties up before the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Uncontested leads can sometimes tempt a horse into a faster-than-intended gallop, and if Colonnade over-exerts by halfway the race turns into a sprint home from a weakening leader; hold-up and late-finishing profiles then come into their own in the final stages. Indian Mary's hold-up style, however compromised by her finishing tendency, and No Ordinary Joe's patient ride could both benefit if the race truly blows apart at the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or both of Mathoura and Dialstone elect to race closer to Colonnade, creating a more competitive pace and a race that rewards those who travel well in the first half.
scenarios.body: With horses engaging Colonnade earlier, the fractions lift enough to test stamina and the winner comes from those who have been handy throughout rather than finishing from far back; Mathoura's solid recent form at this trip on Good ground and Dialstone's consecutive placed runs both suit racing from a prominent position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Upsets Favourites
scenarios.trigger: If Soul Of Appin, whose style and going suitability are unknown, produces an unexpectedly strong debut or return performance and catches the field flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Lightly raced types with unknown profiles occasionally spring a surprise when the pace is steady and the race run to suit an undiscovered profile; Jack Callan's track knowledge and Brian Meehan's 3/11 recent form give a small foothold in the argument, but the absence of any form data makes this a low-probability outlier.

watchPoints.text: Colonnade's early pace: watch whether Jack Mitchell settles him comfortably or allows him to travel faster than ideal given the step up from 8f — if he idles in front the race stays steadily run; if he fights the bridle the pace lifts sharply.

Soul Of Appin's pre-race behaviour and early positioning in the stalls: as an unknown quantity with no form lines, any sign of inexperience or erratic break from the gate could directly shape how the small field orders itself through the first furlong.

Indian Mary's finishing tendency is flagged — if she fails to improve her position from the home turn and once again fades, this confirms the hold-up profile as unsuitable for Bath's uphill finish and removes her from calculations entirely.

Mathoura's draw in stall 3 and Dialstone in stall 2 place both danger horses on the inside of Colonnade (stall 4) at the start; watch whether either opts to push up and race alongside Colonnade early, which would immediately transform the tempo from steady to genuinely contested.

No Ordinary Joe's trip profile is worth monitoring — his most recent wins came at 20f and 15f, and at ten years old racing 1m2f represents a substantial cut in distance; if he is being aimed at a confidence run or a fit-up before a return to staying trips, his market moves should be treated with caution.

runners_data.name: Cracking Idea
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 2yo showed ability with a third on debut over 7f on Good, and holds legitimate claims on that form, but is a natural hold-up operator whose true style cannot be accommodated at the rear in this field — effective chance depends on whether pace collapse turns midfield into the optimal spot today.

runners_data.name: Biscaysian
runners_data.note: Prominent-running Michael Bell 2yo with two runs on Good ground at 7f-8f and placed on the Scorecard as a leading danger; both runs came on similar going and the step to a mile could suit a horse that has looked one-paced rather than non-staying.

runners_data.name: Baarberini
runners_data.note: Midfield type with consecutive placed efforts at 7f-8f on Soft and Standard, so the step to Good ground at Bath is an unknown but James Horton's runner is travelling in on decent form and the mile trip looks a fair test for a horse finishing in the frame consistently.

runners_data.name: Able Tasman
runners_data.note: Scorecard top selection with high confidence; Jack Mitchell takes the ride for Archie Watson's operation, the single Good-going run produced a third over 7f, and as the confirmed front-runner from draw 4 he is ideally placed to try to control tempo and get first run on the field into the straight.

runners_data.name: Yabreen
runners_data.note: Finished seventh on debut over 6f on Good for Jack Channon, so the step up to a mile here is significant and represents an open question about stamina; hold-up style leaves this runner dependent on others doing the donkey work.

runners_data.name: Orchard Hatches
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from a wide draw of 12, which could mean being outpaced across to the rail by Able Tasman from stall 4, creating a pace contest that burns both; Marcus Tregoning's 2yo has produced a place and an eighth in two runs on Good and sets up the race for others if the duel proves too costly.

runners_data.name: Deira Moon
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's debutant-like runner carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag plus a 61-day break, and the only run (seventh over 7f on Soft) gives limited confidence on Good turf at this longer trip; hold-up style with a finishing concern is a difficult combination.

runners_data.name: The Sergeon
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's runner finished fifth over 8f on Good last time and races in a hold-up style from draw 10; the apprentice Jack Dace (5lb) is a factor to weigh, but form to date shows no particular reason to single out against stronger-profile rivals.

runners_data.name: Starlight Bay
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish warning and a run of zero (likely pulled up or last) on Soft over 8f; only 14 days since that effort for Marcus Tregoning, and the going switch to Good may help marginally, but the combination of flags makes this hard to enthuse about from draw 2.

runners_data.name: Naseebwali
runners_data.note: Unraced, unknown going preference, unknown style flagged as UNKNOWN — Michael Keady's runner is a pure unknown quantity and must be treated as such until shown otherwise.

runners_data.name: Boomshakalak
runners_data.note: Zoe Hawkins's 2yo finished seventh over 7f on Good and has a fades-in-finish flag; a natural hold-up type who, like Cracking Idea, has been pushed into the midfield map zone because the field is too heavily hold-up loaded at the rear — that style compromise, combined with the finishing concern, markedly limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Greta Tintin
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's prominent-style runner finished 13th and 9th on Soft and Standard, so form is poor, though this is clearly a well-bred yard with the capacity to improve; draw 14 is the widest in the field and will require Carver to work across early if committed to a forward position.

runners_data.name: Trispen
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows sends out an unraced 2yo with style and going both listed as UNKNOWN from draw 11; Burrows can place a debutant well and the yard's 14-day record of 3/14 is respectable, but there is no form to assess.

runners_data.name: Mulvaney's Return
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's prominent runner has placed third over 8f on Soft and sixth over 8f on Good, giving genuine course-trip relevance; the nine-day turnaround is brisk but connections evidently feel the horse is ready, and prominent style suits the expected race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Orchard Hatches and Able Tasman are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both drawn on the far side of the field (draws 12 and 4 respectively) they will push forward immediately, creating a genuinely contested early gallop over Bath's mile that begins with a climb before the downhill run to the home straight. The pace contest between these two ensures the race will not be falsely run — an honest, even tempo is likely, which on Good turf at Bath over a mile classically stretches the field and sets up the straight for closers and prominent horses who have settled just off the speed. Biscaysian and Mulvaney's Return, both prominent types, are the likeliest to benefit from sitting second or third, close enough to the pace without burning energy early, while the true hold-up horses such as Cracking Idea and Boomshakalak have been mapped to midfield by the tool because there are more hold-up types in this field than the race can accommodate at the rear — those two are unlikely to secure their natural deep position. The tactical verdict favours prominent/mid-division horses who can travel comfortably behind the two pacemakers and pick up in the straight, with pure closers at a structural disadvantage given the congested back-of-field and the redistribution of natural hold-up types into that space.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace duel, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Orchard Hatches and Able Tasman push each other along from the front and the honest gallop softens both inside the final furlong, allowing a settled prominent or mid-division horse to sweep past.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace off the front two plays directly into the hands of horses who have travelled in behind without expending energy, and as the pacemakers tire approaching the home straight the prominent and midfield runners with the cleanest finishing kick will emerge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Able Tasman dictates and wins
scenarios.trigger: If Able Tasman establishes clean, uncontested control early and Orchard Hatches fails to match him stride for stride, leaving Able Tasman to dictate an unrushed gallop that suits a relaxed front-runner.
scenarios.body: Racing from draw 4, Able Tasman could slot across and lead at a measured pace that preserves stamina, and Archie Watson's runner — the only horse in the Scorecard's top selection — has Good-going form and the profile to win from the front if left alone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield types pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel between Orchard Hatches and Able Tasman is fierce enough to collapse both and leave the race open for midfield runners to run through beaten horses in the straight.
scenarios.body: Baarberini has hit the frame twice and handles this trip, while Mulvaney's Return has course-trip experience and the prominent-to-midfield profile to be finishing strongly as the front pair fold.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers pounce from rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unsustainably fast, opening a late window for true hold-up types to storm home from well back.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally compromised because Cracking Idea and Boomshakalak — the natural closers — have been redistributed into midfield given the crowded hold-up quarter, meaning neither is likely to get far enough back to produce a genuinely devastating late run; only a genuine pace collapse would activate this shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Able Tasman or Orchard Hatches secures the lead uncontested — if Orchard Hatches (draw 12) forces a genuine duel from wide, both front-runners could be compromised and the race will open up dramatically for Biscaysian and Mulvaney's Return to sweep past.

Cracking Idea and Boomshakalak are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield by the tool — if either jockey tries to drop the horse back to its natural position at the rear, watch for traffic issues and a late, possibly insufficient, run that arrives too late on the flat home straight.

Greta Tintin from draw 14 is prominent-style but must cover extra ground from the outside — if Carver cannot find a pitch close to the pace early, the Andrew Balding runner could be burning energy without reward over a trip that already exposes the horse's modest recent form.

Naseebwali and Trispen are both unraced and unknown — watch the market move in the hour before the race, as significant support for either debutant would suggest strong stable confidence that the form data cannot currently capture.

Baarberini drops from Soft/Standard to Good turf for James Horton — if the horse travels strongly through the mid-stages and produces a clean challenge in the Bath straight, it would signal the going switch has unlocked improvement not visible in the form figures.

races.paceDynamic: Amber Ocean is the confirmed front-runner and will look to dictate from stall 8, but faces an immediate disadvantage on a course where low draws dominate — she must work hard from the outside to secure the rail line, which could burn petrol before the race truly begins. Behind her, Dowman, Perigord Noir, Space Dreamer, and PJ's Corner all want prominent positions, meaning there will be genuine scrapping for territory in the opening furlong even at a nominally sustainable pace, with traffic compression likely between the two- and three-furlong markers. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically all hold their position, with Amber Ocean and Perigord Noir best placed to actually secure the positions they want given pace commitment and draw respectively — PJ's Corner and Space Dreamer from stalls 10 and 9 face the steepest climb. A genuinely contested early pace on Good ground over a flat 5f at Bath, with draw bias strongly in play, tilts the tactical verdict firmly in favour of the prominent racer settled just off the early battle who can pounce in the final furlong from a favoured low draw.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Perigord Noir Stalks and Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Amber Ocean sets a pressured early pace from stall 8 that drains the field while Perigord Noir settles prominently from stall 2 and swoops in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Amber Ocean's outside draw forces her to work to find her position and the contested early fractions leave the leader vulnerable in the closing stages on flat Bath ground. Perigord Noir benefits from the rail-side draw, a 14-day fresh return, and a prominent style that gets it into the race without burning energy, arriving at the crucial moment with most left.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Amber Ocean Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners fail to sustain their challenge and Amber Ocean — despite the draw — establishes a comfortable lead early and is never seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: Amber Ocean has the early pace and class to dictate on Good ground where the fractions remain honest rather than punishing, and the front-running form is proven across similar trips. If the prominent pack split and cancel each other out chasing wide, Amber Ocean could steal enough daylight to hold off all challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a cavalry charge and a midfield tracker times a late run to catch the tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Penny Capri (draw 3, midfield style, recent 5f Good winner) is ideally positioned from a favoured low draw to pick up the pieces if front-runners overcook things, and Knock Three Times also holds claims if the pace truly blows up. Good ground does not typically produce the extreme collapse needed, keeping this scenario a minority chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop from Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely scorching and true hold-up runners pounce down the outside in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Jazz Queen from stall 1 has the ideal draw for a hold-up closer but has shown no win form and consistently finishes mid-pack, while Birkacre Brow is naturally a prominent type redistributed to the rear and is unlikely to deliver a genuine late swoop out of role. This shape demands horses that are authentic hold-up types, and this field has very few — probability is correspondingly low.

watchPoints.text: Amber Ocean (stall 8) must cross the field to find the rail on a course with a strong low-draw bias — watch the first furlong for how much she has to work, as it directly determines whether she can control the race.

Perigord Noir and Dowman both want the prominent position from low draws — if they race against each other in the early stages rather than tracking Amber Ocean, both risks being too far back when it matters.

PJ's Corner and Space Dreamer from stalls 10 and 9 will struggle to replicate their prominent-race style against the draw bias; watch whether they chase wide or drop back — either way the bias is working against them.

Birkacre Brow is tagged as redistributed to hold-up despite being a natural prominent type; watch whether it pushes forward early, as it may add to the prominent congestion rather than filling the hold-up role the field mapping assigns it.

With Good ground confirmed across all races on the card and no significant drying out, expect normal Bath 5f times with no surface outlier — pace-setters who waste energy early on this flat track will feel it in the final 100 yards.

runners_data.note: Scorecard's top selection: Michael Wigham's five-year-old has a strong recent form line of 1-2-3 over 14-16f on good ground, wears a visor, and jockey Alexandra Egan (7lb claim) helps offset the top weight; the midfield style suits a well-run staying race at Bath perfectly.|

races.paceDynamic: Smith and Lady Lauren are the two confirmed front-runners here, and with both likely to press for the early lead over 2m1f on good ground at Bath, the race should be run at an honest, even gallop from the outset — neither is a dominant, class-above pacesetter, so the tempo will be genuine rather than suicidal. The long Bath straight and good ground will see this develop into a thorough test of stamina, with the pace honest enough to expose any stayer who lacks the engine to sustain effort into the final quarter-mile. This shape strongly favours a horse with a reliable, well-positioned midfield cruising style that can track the pace without expending energy, then produce a sustained — rather than sudden — finishing effort; Fram Castle's profile fits that template precisely. The field contains more hold-up types than the rear of the field can accommodate: La Trinite, Fornido, Cherry Cola, and N'Ion are all genuine hold-up horses shuffled into midfield on the map, with Simiyann and Chillhi also likely to be further back than ideal, meaning those who can sit closer to a genuine gallop hold a clear positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest pace, Fram Castle cruises
scenarios.trigger: If Smith and Lady Lauren set a true, sustained gallop that strings the field out and rewards horses who track the pace efficiently.
scenarios.body: Fram Castle, racing from a natural midfield position, tracks the leaders without drama over the long 2m1f trip and produces a sustained staying effort up the Bath straight that the hold-up brigade cannot match from their compromised positions; the good ground and even tempo suit a horse whose five-run form string shows 1-2-3 finishes over similar trips in similar conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, closers sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Smith and Lady Lauren go too hard early and capitulate before two furlongs out, leaving a vacuum for hold-up horses to fill.
scenarios.body: A strong early pace burns up both front-runners turning for home, and horses who have been able to settle and conserve energy in the final third of the field get a clean run through to capitalise; Simiyann, who consistently finishes in the places and handles good ground well, would be the primary beneficiary, with La Trinite's hold-up style finally suiting the race shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow early, front pair slog on
scenarios.trigger: If Smith and Lady Lauren fail to push on significantly and the field bunches, gifting the pace-setters an uncontested lead at a modest tempo.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race over this marathon trip at Bath would allow the front pair to conserve enough energy to hold on as the hold-up horses find themselves with insufficient ground to reel them in; Lady Lauren, despite modest form figures, is the younger and more unexposed of the two and could benefit most from dictating a slow-then-sprint scenario, though Smith's experience over staying trips is a countervailing factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield scrapper nicks it
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest but Fram Castle fails to quicken, allowing a prominent-to-midfield rival to grind past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Cloudy Rose or Fornido — both pushed into midfield by congestion rather than natural preference — manage to find a competitive position from which they can sustain a run through the final two furlongs on good ground; this is the least likely shape because several of the nominal midfield runners are redistributed hold-up horses whose true style puts them further back, thinning the genuine positional competition for Fram Castle.

watchPoints.text: Fornido has posted four consecutive fourth-place finishes and trainer Attwater has a T14 strike of 1/13 — if the pace is strong enough to bring hold-up runners into play late, this horse's place consistency makes it the most credible threat to Fram Castle among the redistribution group.

Smith's 68-day absence combined with a 0/3 trainer T14 record means the front-runner's fitness and stamina over 2m1f is unproven on this return — if Smith fades earlier than expected, the pace could become falsely strung out and disrupt the anticipated even gallop.

Turton is stepping up dramatically in trip from 8-10f to 2m1f; if he fails to settle in the early stages alongside the two confirmed front-runners, he could unbalance the pace and create an erratic early tempo that scrambles the race shape.

Simiyann and La Trinite are both trained by Ian Williams (T14: 2/27) — watch whether stable tactics involve one horse being ridden as a pacifier to set things up for the other, or whether they simply run their own races from different positions in the field.

Alexandra Egan's 7lb claim on Fram Castle is worth monitoring in the context of a long, stamina-sapping 2m1f — if the claim is used aggressively to hold a prominent pitch from draw 2, it could prove decisive in a race where positional advantage over this trip is at a premium.

runners_data.name: Alshimali
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Good 6f and has finishing form at this level, but stall 6 is against the draw bias and Josephine Gordon will need to find cover quickly; true hold-up style suits a slow-tempo scenario more than the likely controlled-but-honest pace here.

runners_data.name: Trafalger
runners_data.note: The race-shaper and sole confirmed front-runner — form reads 35-855, meaning his recent record in similar Good ground 5-6f contests is uninspiring at best (four times beaten into fifth or worse), and he carries 135lbs; expect him to lead but there is a genuine risk he flatters to deceive before the sharp finish.

runners_data.name: May Encounter
runners_data.note: Stall 2 provides a meaningful draw advantage but five consecutive runs without placing and a form string of -55647 make it hard to get enthusiastic; hold-up style from a favoured draw is a small tactical positive, though the weight of evidence points to limited ability at this level.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Mid-draw stall 3, midfield style, blinkered, and has placed four times on Good ground from ten similar-going runs — the consistency angle is real; trainer Rod Millman is ticking over at 2/24 over 14 days, which is modest, but this is a horse that keeps finding the frame rather than winning.

runners_data.name: Ten Club
runners_data.note: Freshest in the field at just 10 days since last run, but an 8/6f/GOO effort is the standout recent run and stall 8 compounds the against-draw flag; in reality a genuine closing type whose true rear-tracking role is squeezed in this small field — the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.93 reflects that racing in a false mid-pack position undermines its best chance.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old with four places in six recent Good-ground starts — remarkably consistent at this level and Egan's 7lb claim brings the weight down meaningfully; prominent style from stall 4 is a decent fit for the expected race shape, and this horse is the most battle-hardened runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Macarone
runners_data.note: Stall 1 is the key asset — the most favoured draw in the race — and Ben Ffrench Davis's 5lb claim helps offset the handicap weight; won last time over 6f on Good ground and has prominent style to go with the positional advantage, all of which aligns directly with how Bath 5½f handicaps tend to be won.

runners_data.name: Rock Master
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, and all five recent runs have been over 7-8f — dropping sharply in trip here is a significant concern; stall 7 is against the draw bias, and apprentice Myla Coppins faces a tough task coaxing a positive showing from a horse that has never looked comfortable at sprint distances.

races.paceDynamic: Trafalger is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn in stall 5, will look to dictate from the outset on Good ground over 5½f at Bath — a track where left-side draws carry a meaningful edge. With no genuine pace rival to pressure him, Trafalger is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo rather than a suicidal gallop, which typically compresses the finish and rewards horses tracking close to the pace rather than closing from deep. Macarone (stall 1, favoured draw) and Some Nightmare (stall 4) are the natural prominent types best positioned to sit just off the leader and pounce, while Be An Angel from stall 3 occupies a workable midfield position. Ten Club is a genuine hold-up horse remapped to midfield because the field holds more closing types than the race shape can absorb at the rear — in a steadily-run race, its true deep-closer role is compromised, and its stall 8 against-draw draw compounds the issue. The tactical verdict favours prominent, left-draw profiles: a moderate front-running tempo over this trip at Bath almost always sees the race won by a horse tracking the leader from a handy position, and Macarone from stall 1 sits at the intersection of favoured draw, prominent style, and recent course-going form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trafalger controls, prominent pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Trafalger goes unchallenged to the front and sets a comfortable, honest but unspectacular pace that sets up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Macarone and Some Nightmare track the leader from handy positions, and the good ground rewards their prominent, forward-travelling style as the race quickens inside the final furlong; the favoured left draw amplifies Macarone's advantage throughout the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady pace, hold-up gets in
scenarios.trigger: If Trafalger crawls early and the tempo becomes genuinely slow, compressing the field and gifting late movers a slice of the pace.
scenarios.body: Alshimali, who has winning form on Good ground, closes from off the pace and catches the leaders flat-footed in the final 100 yards; the hold-up horses benefit only if the pace is genuinely sub-standard rather than merely comfortable, making this the second-most plausible shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Draw bias dominates throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the low-draw advantage proves unusually pronounced on the day and the race is effectively decided by position from the gate.
scenarios.body: Macarone from stall 1 and May Encounter from stall 2 secure the rail and are never headed in terms of track position; May Encounter's flat record at the trip is modest but the rail draw provides a significant mechanical edge that can outweigh raw ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, chaotic finish
scenarios.trigger: If Trafalger is taken on early or finds the 5½f trip too sharp and fades, leaving the race without a true pacer and causing a bunched, unpredictable conclusion.
scenarios.body: Rock Master, though flagged as a horse that fades in finishes and has been running over longer distances, could momentarily benefit from a muddling pace before lack of stamina becomes irrelevant; Ten Club's redistribution away from its natural closing role and its high stall make a winning intervention very unlikely even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Macarone's stall 1 draw combined with a prominent style and recent 6f Good ground win makes this horse the one to physically track from the gate — if it secures the rail and travels kindly, rivals may struggle to pass.

Trafalger's record of five defeats in Good-ground 5-6f races despite being the sole front-runner suggests the pace it sets could be beatable — watch whether Some Nightmare or Macarone are close enough to overtake if Trafalger weakens in the final furlong.

Ten Club's true hold-up profile is compromised by being mapped artificially into midfield — if it drops to its natural position at the rear from stall 8, it faces an extremely difficult task against the draw bias and may post another below-par effort.

Alshimali is trained by Tony Carroll, who shares the yard with Rock Master and is running at 5/41 over 14 days — neither horse is in a form cluster suggesting yard momentum, though Alshimali's Good ground winning form gives it a specific scenario where it can threaten.

Rock Master's form entirely over 7-8f with a consistent fade flag means any signs of travelling strongly early should be treated with caution — it is unlikely to sustain its effort over the final furlong of a 5½f test.

runners_data.name: The Ormer Gatherer
runners_data.note: 456 days off the track and lightly raced with an unknown style flag — the long absence combined with a trainer strike rate of 2/11 over 14 days makes this a near-impossible profile to assess; extreme caution warranted.

runners_data.name: Nammos
runners_data.note: Strand top selection racing in midfield from a neutral stall 9; recent form shows consistent placed efforts at 7-8f on Good ground and this pace shape suits his style, though trainer has returned 0/7 over 14 days and he wears headgear (p); last ran 12 days ago.

runners_data.name: Hopjes
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-tie and blinkers and has been running over much longer trips (16-18f) than today's mile — a significant drop in distance is the headline concern, and this natural hold-up horse is one of three closers the map has pushed into midfield given the dearth of true pace in the field.

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on class (OR 62) with three wins in her last six starts all on Good ground; her trainer Tony Carroll is operating at 5/41 over 14 days and she handles this trip and going well — straightforward favourite profile who can run from a handy midfield berth.

runners_data.name: Ravenglass
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a hold-up style who ideally wants to close from off the pace, but in a race this light on pace, finding a clean run from the back is the core risk; carries headgear (p) and drew stall 8, which won't help him manufacture his preferred position.

runners_data.name: Green Icon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form shows a best of 3rd over 8f on Good, with several poor efforts at shorter; stall 7 is neutral and Millie Wonnacott (5lb claimer) takes off enough weight to remain competitive in handicap terms, but the finishing form is limited.

runners_data.name: Victorian Rose
runners_data.note: Prominent-style filly with a clear fade flag in the finishing section; form reads 800 in three starts, all on softer or all-weather, and this is a step up in class — the draw in stall 11 is manageable but the overall profile is weak.

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose best effort in the last five runs was a 4th over 6f on Standard — today's step up to a mile on Good ground is an unknown; wears a hood (b) and the 0/3 trainer strike rate over 14 days adds little confidence.

runners_data.name: Arvana Belle
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed three times from nine Good-ground starts and drew stall 1, meaning she should get a clean prominent pitch from the outset — her profile is suited to a controlled-tempo race where handy types can press through the turn.

runners_data.name: Grand Vista
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best runs have come over 7-8f on Good ground with two places from nine recent starts; Daniel Muscutt is an upgrade in the saddle and he placed 3rd over 8f on Good, but the closing profile is less favoured by this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Strand danger who won over 8f on Good recently and operates as a genuine hold-up horse from stall 4; the Good ground is confirmed fine and a consistent recent form string (136 in last three) makes her the most credible late challenger if any pace materialises.

runners_data.name: Oh So Audacious
runners_data.note: A genuine closer by nature, but with three redistributed hold-up horses mapped into midfield in this race, Oh So Audacious is among those unlikely to secure their preferred deep-lying position; all seven recent runs have come on Good ground (0W) and the stall-3 draw does not help him slide back.

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Strand danger who won over 7f on Soft last time and has placed three times from five Good-ground starts; racing hold-up from an outside draw (14) is workable and her form is genuinely live, though the step from 7f to a mile and the trainer's 1/21 14-day record are minor negatives.

runners_data.name: Neat And Tidy
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner who will set the tempo from stall 12 — the wide draw means she must work across early, and while she has a style-fit discount (0.94) for racing outside her clearest comfort zone, she is still the only horse guaranteed to shape the race from the front; no wins in recent form but could steal it if pace is slow enough.

races.paceDynamic: Neat And Tidy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace-presser likely to challenge for the lead, should settle comfortably on the bridle through a measured tempo on Good ground over Bath's turning mile. Victorian Rose holds a prominent pitch but has a fade flag and is unlikely to put Neat And Tidy under any meaningful pressure, meaning fractions will be controlled rather than breakneck. This shape — a lone, unhurried leader setting a sustainable gallop — classically compresses the race into a single surge from the home turn, where horses racing in the first half of the field with a strong finishing kick hold a decisive edge over those trapped deep in a slowly-run queue. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically operate from their natural position: Ravenglass, Hopjes, and Oh So Audacious are genuine closers pushed into a midfield mapping, but in a race with only one genuine pace-setter and a controlled tempo, their ability to secure a meaningful advantage over the final two furlongs is compromised. The tactical verdict is clear: a prominent-to-midfield profile with proven Good-ground finishing speed is the profile to be with, as the race is likely to be won from a handy position rather than from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Neat And Tidy dictates a steady tempo unchallenged and the race turns into a sprint from the home bend.
scenarios.body: Nammos, sitting comfortably in midfield, can travel into the race efficiently and produce a sustained run from two out, exactly the shape this good-ground miler has shown he handles; Shes Got The Blues, with her strong recent form and Good-ground wins, will also be produced from a handy position to challenge late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally faster than expected, creating enough tempo for true closers to reel in the principals.
scenarios.body: Angel's Call, a genuine winner at this trip on Good ground and racing from a hold-up berth, would have the most realistic closing profile if the gallop quickens; A Rose Adaay showed strong form last time and can produce a sustained late run if the pace is honest enough to bring her into it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Neat And Tidy takes control at a crawl and the field fails to organise a meaningful challenge through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Racing out of role relative to recent form, Neat And Tidy would need the race to fall completely his way with no one prepared to go after him — Victorian Rose from draw 11 offers token pressure but fades; Arvana Belle, sitting just off the lead from stall 1, could also pinch a place if her prominent style is rewarded by a falsely-run contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsiders Land
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo collapses entirely and a wide-open late sprint produces a shock result from an unexpected quarter.
scenarios.body: Shes Got The Blues has the best raw form on Good ground across the field and would still finish prominently; Medyg, who has shown ability at the trip despite modest recent returns, is the type who could benefit from complete chaos in the closing stages if the race breaks unusually.

watchPoints.text: Neat And Tidy drawn wide in stall 12 — watch how quickly she crosses to find a rail line early, as any significant energy expenditure getting across the field before settling in front could undermine her ability to sustain the pace through the home turn.

Angel's Call and A Rose Adaay are both Strand-flagged dangers operating as hold-up types — if either gets shuffled wide or loses momentum on the home bend, the late challenge that makes them dangerous evaporates in a slowly-run race.

Shes Got The Blues carries the highest OR in the field (62) and is clearly well-treated on form, but her 5lb penalty from the claimer and the Bath mile's turning nature mean watch whether she can get a clear passage from stall 10 without being hampered mid-race.

Hopjes is entering from a dramatically longer trip (16-18f last five starts) down to a mile — any signs of early exuberance or the jockey riding her forward would be a significant tell, as she is not built for this kind of pace test based on recent assignments.

The three redistributed closers (Ravenglass, Hopjes, Oh So Audacious) will be worth watching at the start — if any of them push forward unexpectedly and inject pace into the early stages, the entire race shape changes from the controlled single-pace scenario that currently dominates the probability.

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Three-year-old midfield filly who showed promise on Good going earlier in her career but has since failed to convert across six attempts; Adrian Wintle's T14 strike rate is modest at 1/17, the step up to a mile is untested, and her sim-going record of 0W0P on Good turf makes it hard to be enthusiastic.

runners_data.name: Typeface
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old with two places in eight Good-ground runs and a 52-day absence to overcome; Ian Williams has a reasonable T14 record (2/27) and the horse handles this trip well, but the layoff and reliance on a truly-run pace to close into make this a watch-and-see at best.

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner and therefore the key pace-setter for the whole race; her Good-going form shows six runs at 6-8f without a win, and she sets the tempo from stall 6 — if unchallenged she becomes more dangerous, but her finishing record (0W1P sim-going) suggests she tends to tire.

runners_data.name: Freedom Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent four-year-old who won over 8f on Good and placed at 10f on the same surface; stall 5 gives Kieran O'Neill an excellent chance to slot into second or third behind Who Is Alice, and the Strand Scorecard's top selection sits in the structurally favoured position for this race shape — the trainer T14 of 0/1 is the only mild negative.

runners_data.name: Desert Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old with an excellent Good-going record (2W3P in five), carrying top weight of 135lbs but comfortably the classiest form figure in the field on similar ground; Daniel Muscutt takes over and could deliver a strong late run if the pace scenario creates enough of a gap.

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old prominent type who has placed three times at 8f on Good and Firm; stall 10 is workable but his 0W record and modest sim-going strike rate (3/14) make him a solid each-way framer at best rather than a race-shaper.

runners_data.name: Amarachi
runners_data.note: Prominent four-year-old who has placed twice at 8f on Stansted (soft-ish) but has a worrying sim-going record on Good (just 1 run, no place); Jack Mitchell takes over for Joseph Parr and the horse's natural style should see him chase Who Is Alice, though his form on this surface type is unproven.

runners_data.name: Savvi Row
runners_data.note: Three-year-old midfield type returning from a 212-day absence, all four previous runs came on Standard (AW) going; the lack of turf form and long absence make assessment almost impossible and he must be treated with extreme caution until he shows his well-being on this surface.

runners_data.name: Mooretown Lad
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose authentic racing style is hold-up — he naturally comes from off the pace — but with so many hold-up types in this field he is squeezed into a midfield map slot that may not reflect where he actually races; Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim helps, but his Good-going record (0W0P in four) and 46-day layoff temper expectations regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Quite Sweet
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old for Tony Carroll (excellent T14 at 5/41) with a placed run on Good going; her form string (60949) includes two poor efforts and a 9th on Good, and while Carroll's yard is in form, Quite Sweet will need everything to go right from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Lady V
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly who has raced exclusively at 6-7f and now steps up to a mile for the first time; her Going record on Good shows two runs and no place and the extra furlong is a significant unknown — Kieren Fox's experience is a mild positive.

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type in stall 1 with a clear ⚠ flag for fading in finishes; Millie Wonnacott takes the ride and the wide draw makes it harder for him to stalk the rail — his Bath form is limited and the fade pattern at a mile is a serious structural concern on a course that rewards those who stay on.

runners_data.name: Girls Allowed
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent filly with a place at 7f on Good and a 19-day turnaround; Julia & Shelley Birkett have a T14 of 1/5 and Dylan Hogan can be effective, but her Good-going record (4/5) includes no wins and she remains a maiden stepping up slightly in trip.

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Prominent four-year-old with only 2 days since last run — the very short turnaround is the standout flag; his Good-going form shows a 7th of 6 at 6f and a poor 10th, and while Jack Dace's claim helps on weight, the fatigue risk from racing two days ago significantly undermines his chance.

races.paceDynamic: Who Is Alice is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 14 and, with prominent rivals Rival, Eye Of The Water, Amarachi, Girls Allowed, and Freedom Bay all pressing toward the head of affairs, the early stages will see a congested battle for position before the race settles into a genuine but not suicidal pace on Bath's turning mile. Who Is Alice's draw in stall 6 gives her a reasonable chance to establish her position, but the six prominent types funnelling into a single-file approach through Bath's early bends will create traffic flashpoints two to three furlongs out as the field fans wider. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can all secure their natural position — Freedom Bay and Amarachi are most likely to actually settle into a prominent berth, while Rival (who fades in finishes and draws widest in stall 1) and Eye Of The Water are the likeliest to be shuffled back against their instincts. A genuinely-run pace on Good turf with no dead-rubber section favours horses who can sit just off the leader or in midfield and produce a sustained, rather than explosive, late run — the Prominent-to-Midfield profile holds the clearest structural advantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Bay Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent pack settles behind her without incident, allowing Freedom Bay to track in second or third.
scenarios.body: Freedom Bay's recent course-and-distance form (2nd and 1st at 8f on Good) is perfectly suited to a race run at a sustainable tempo where a prominent stalker can pick off the leader entering the final furlong; Kieran O'Neill's ability to get a comfortable pitch from stall 5 is a key enabler.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Aids Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack races keenly and jostle for position into the first bend, burning enough energy to set up a late run for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Desert Charm's strong record on Good going (2W, 3P in last five) and hold-up style means he arrives late with fresh legs if the pace is genuinely quick early; Typeface, who has placed twice at this trip on Good, is another horse capable of closing from off the pace if the race shape suits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice gets a soft lead without serious pressure and the prominent challengers fail to coordinate a meaningful pursuit.
scenarios.body: At a sustainable Bath mile gallop with no one willing to take her on early, Who Is Alice could simply conserve enough energy to resist, particularly if those behind her get into traffic issues two furlongs out; Harry Vigors's claim helps offset the weight and the soft-ish front-runner profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent contest ties itself in knots and a hold-up type from a wider draw produces an unimpeded late challenge.
scenarios.body: Thai Princess (stall 2, midfield style, one similar-going placing) and Quite Sweet could both find a clean passage if the rail-side runners cause interference, though neither has the form profile to make this consistently reliable.

watchPoints.text: Coiled ran just two days ago — monitor in the paddock and market for signs of stiffness or dullness, as the ultra-short turnaround at a mile on turf is a significant red flag for soundness and performance.

Prominent congestion across Rival, Eye Of The Water, Amarachi, Girls Allowed, and Freedom Bay will create a scrimmage for position at Bath's first bend — any horse on the wrong side of a bump or shuffle 1-2 furlongs in could be fatally compromised.

Who Is Alice's hold headgear (hg:h) is noted but her pace data shows her as the field's sole front-runner — watch whether she actually bowls straight to the front or if an unexpected rival (Girls Allowed, Rival) attempts to race her for the lead, which would dramatically change the tempo.

Freedom Bay's trainer Zoe Hawkins has only one runner in the T14 window (0/1) — if market confidence collapses on race morning it could signal something amiss, but the horse's structural position and form on Good ground make it a watch rather than an automatic concern.

Savvi Row returns from 212 days off with all prior form on All-Weather Standard going — watch how quickly he is backed or drifts in the market as any late support would imply Millman's team is happy with his turf readiness.
